strengths_deep_dive: Primary operational strengths center on low direct fundraising costs and direct allocation of spent funds. According to filed records, the charity maintained a <cite id="3">Program expense ratio of 92.5% in FY2024</cite>, surpassing the 75% industry standard [3]. Additionally, it reported <cite id="1">$0.00 spent on fundraising per $1 raised</cite>, reflecting minimal donor acquisition costs [1]. Having served the community since being <cite id="2">founded in 1974</cite>, it maintains deep roots in its local region [2].
rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Society of Northwest Suburbs of Chicago operates with severe operational and financial limiting factors. While the organization provides core religious programs, educational offerings, and zakat distribution [2], its primary limiting factor is holding an extraordinary reserve level. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $3,697,122</cite>, yet revenue declined 10% from FY2023 figures ($4,092,615) [3]. Operating with <cite id="1">117.3 months of working capital</cite> (and at least 117.3 months of operating reserves), the charity maintains capital far beyond typical operating requirements [1]. This excessive accumulation of funds poses a direct concern for donors, particularly regarding prompt zakat deployment [2]. Board governance remains unverified with limited transparency data, contributing to its overall low evaluation [1]. As a bright spot behind these financial concerns, the filed figures indicate a <cite id="3">Program expense ratio of 92.5% in FY2024</cite>, alongside <cite id="1">a fundraising efficiency of <$0.01 per $1 raised</cite> [1]. However, overall organizational practices leave substantial room for governance and financial management improvements [1].
